state: You are analyzing a game of standard international chess. The position is: White king on e1, White rook on a1, White pawn on e4; Black king on e8, Black queen on d8, Black knight on g8. It is White to move. Standard FIDE rules apply.

knight_move.instructions: How does a knight move on an empty board?

criteria.l_shape: In an L shape: two squares in one direction then one square perpendicular.
criteria.straight: Any number of squares in a straight line.
criteria.one_any: Exactly one square in any direction.

castling_condition.instructions: In the given position, can White castle kingside this turn?
castling_condition.note: White has no kingside rook and no f1/g1 pieces set up; the h1 rook is absent. Also the king has not moved but there is no h1 rook to castle with.

pawn_first_move.instructions: Can a pawn move two squares forward on its very first move from its starting rank?
pawn_first_move.note: Yes - a pawn may advance two squares from its starting square if both squares are empty.

check_def.instructions: What does it mean for a king to be 'in check'?

criteria.attacked: The king is currently attacked by at least one enemy piece.
criteria.pinned: The king is pinned to another piece.
criteria.stalemated: The king has no legal moves.

promotion_rank.instructions: To which rank must a White pawn reach to promote?

en_passant.instructions: Is capturing en passant a legal move in standard international chess?
en_passant.note: Yes - en passant is available immediately after an enemy pawn makes a two-square advance adjacent to your pawn.

stalemate_result.instructions: If a player has no legal move but their king is not in check, what is the result?

criteria.loss: The player with no moves loses.
criteria.win: The player with no moves wins.

value_queen.instructions: Is a queen generally considered more valuable than a rook?
value_queen.note: Yes - queen is worth about 9 pawns, rook about 5.

bishop_color.instructions: Can a bishop ever change the color of the squares it moves on during a game?
bishop_color.note: No - a bishop stays on one color for the whole game.

board_score.instructions: How strong is a queen relative to the other chess pieces (in standard point values)?
criteria: Weak: worth about as much as a pawn.
Below average: worth about as much as a knight.
Strong: worth more than a bishop but slightly less than a rook.
Very strong: worth substantially more than any other single piece.
